hints.title: Core Idea
hints.text: Find users with at least two consecutive sessions of the same type within 12 hours.

hints.title: Key Observation
hints.text: Partition by user id and session type, ordering by session start to inspect consecutive sessions.

hints.title: Query Structure
hints.text: Use the lag window function to compare current session start with previous session end, filtering differences under 12 hours.

hints.title: Implementation
hints.text:
```mysql
WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        session_start,
        LAG(session_end) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, session_type ORDER BY session_start) AS prev_end
    FROM Sessions
)
SELECT DISTINCT user_id
FROM T
WHERE TIMESTAMPDIFF(SECOND, prev_end, session_start) BETWEEN 0 AND 43200
ORDER BY user_id;
```

complexity.notes: Partition sort with lag window comparison.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Cross-joining sessions without window functions generates O(N^2) comparisons.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Use window functions partitioned by user and session type to check temporal gap.

solutions.approach: Window Lag Partition with Epoch Difference
solutions.code:
WITH T AS (
    SELECT
        user_id,
        session_start,
        LAG(session_end) OVER (PARTITION BY user_id, session_type ORDER BY session_start) AS prev_end
    FROM Sessions
)
SELECT DISTINCT user_id
FROM T
WHERE EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM (session_start - prev_end)) BETWEEN 0 AND 43200
ORDER BY user_id;
